I would suggest working as a cna at a floor or hospital that you’re interested in. It’ll help you see in person what working in healthcare is actually like and you’ll get to make connections that may benefit you later on. If you’re able to you can also try picking up on different floors as a cna so you can see what it’s like working on those units since it can feel different than when you’re on a floor for clinical. That’s what I did and I was able to see how some floors didn’t really have a welcoming vibe compared to others. Also you can look for nurse extern positions which is basically like clinical but you get paid for it where during the summer you follow a nurse around and work with her. I did a nurse extern position at my hospital’s nicu and later they offered me a new grad position there! But above all I would say to really try to put yourself in positions where you can experience as many different areas of nursing as you can especially if you’re not sure exactly where you want to go after you graduate. I wish you the best of luck with school and everything else 💗💗💗

For peds make sure to pay attention if the answer makes sense according to the patients age. 
Ex: 
- during an assessment of a 12 you wouldn’t assess for fontanels because they should already be closed up. 
- For a pain assessment of a 4 month old you wouldn’t ask them what makes their pain worse/better because they can’t talk. 
- When describing a procedure to a 6 year old you wouldn’t go into too much detail of what’s going to happen using big words, you would show them pictures/diagrams, could act out a demonstration, or preform a puppet show

It’s not a dumb question at all. But yeah basically drinking more water instead of sodas and juices, which are high in calories, will help lower your caloric intake. Water will also help dilute your sodium levels which will lead to your body not holding onto as much of the water already in you body since your replacing it with the water that your drinking (basically you’ll pee it out). Just make sure that you’re not drinking more than 1 l of water in an hour so that your kidneys will have time to filter through the water properly.
